metadata.creator: Lucas, Harold V.
metadata.description: Harold V. Lucas writes to the president of Miami University concerning Ming Kong Chong, a student expected to graduate in 1940 and return to Hawaii to work in the public instruction department as a teacher. Lucas offers testimony about Chong's character, leadership, and willingness to help, based on having known him for eight years.
metadata.title: Letter from Harold V. Lucas concerning a Miami University student, 24 April 1940
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
April 24, 1940

President
Miami University
Oxford, Ohio

Dear Sir:

It has come to my attention that a personal note from me might well be of value to you with the character and person of one of your students Ming Kong Chong who, I understand, hopes to be graduated from your University in 1940 with intention of returning to Hawaii to enter the department of public instruction as a teacher here. I am very pleased to send this word of testimony concerning Mr. Chong whom I have known for the past eight years. While I am not qualified to speak for his scholastic ability, I do feel that I know enough of him and his [illegible] to say definitely that he is the type of young man we are hoping [illegible] more and more will enter the public school system here.

I knew Ming Kong when he was in high school and during a summer camp I came to know him even better. His character, I believe, is above reproach. His willingness to be helpful and his leadership even as a boy was very definitely an asset to the camp. In [illegible] during his years on the mainland, he has continued on the path I knew him to follow. I am sure he will be a splendid teacher and friend to young people.

Very cordially yours,

Harold V. Lucas,
GENERAL SECRETARY YMCA [Young Men's Christian Association]

[illegible]
